references.text: The first census in Israel at Sinai, where the same command was given to count all men from twenty years old and upward who could go out to war.
Describes how the people were gathered and registered by their clans, from twenty years old and upward.
The result of the first census, where all Israelites from twenty years old and upward who could go out to war were counted.
The basis for the census: everyone from twenty years old and upward was to give a ransom to the Lord.
Refers to the counting of all men from twenty years old and upward at the building of the tabernacle.
Judgment on the first generation: all from twenty years old and upward who had grumbled were to die in the wilderness, which explains the need for a new census.
David's census followed the same principle with an age limit of twenty years.
